claim: Monitoring cadence for NVMe/SSD health must match the failure mode: per-second to 60-second intervals for thermal spikes and media-error bursts, daily/weekly for slow endurance trends - with reference defaults being Netdata NVMe collector 10s, smartctl_exporter 60s (with 10-min device rescan), Zabbix SMART template 6 hours, Scrutiny daily cron.
stance_target: Poll-interval selection for ha-linux-agent's storage/system collectors on jupiterOS fleet hosts
quoted_support: Match the cadence to the failure mode. Real-time monitoring at per-second to 60-second intervals catches thermal spikes and media error bursts as they happen. Daily or weekly audits are enough for slow-moving endurance and spare-capacity trends. For reference: Scrutiny defaults to daily collection, the Zabbix SMART template refreshes every 6 hours, smartctl_exporter polls every 60 seconds, and the Netdata NVMe collector defaults to 10 seconds.

claim: NVMe drives expose a different health information log (percentage used, available spare, media errors, critical-warning bitfield) instead of ATA-style SMART attributes, so tools that parse ATA attributes show incomplete or empty data for NVMe drives - a tool must read the NVMe log natively.
stance_target: ha-linux-agent's storage collector must parse the NVMe health log (via nvme-cli/smartctl JSON), not an ATA SMART parser
scope_conditions: NVMe vs SATA/SAS SMART semantics; smartmontools documentation
quoted_support: NVMe uses a different health information log, not ATA-style SMART attributes. Instead of reallocated sector counts and vendor-specific fields, NVMe exposes percentage used, available spare, media errors, and a critical warning bitfield. smartmontools notes that NVMe drives do not provide ATA-style vendor attributes at all.

claim: Netdata's NVMe collector requires nvme-cli and privileged access (ndsudo) per host with a 10-second default interval and a built-in critical-warnings alert, while its separate smartctl-based SMART collector has no default alerts and no auto-detection (manual device selectors) - and per-metric thresholds are the user's job on every platform except Zabbix's template triggers (endurance >90%, high temp, smartctl exit bits).
stance_target: Even incumbent agents require privileged helper access for storage health - relevant to ha-linux-agent's privilege/sandboxing design on NixOS
scope_conditions: Netdata NVMe/SMART collectors, Zabbix agent 2 template; vendor comparison page (Netdata-authored)
quoted_support: The NVMe collector needs nvme-cli installed and privileged access (ndsudo) on each host, and the SMART collector does not auto-detect devices - you configure device selectors or extra devices. Only the NVMe critical-warnings alert ships built in; the SMART collector has no default alerts, so you define your own thresholds.

claim: Prometheus smartctl_exporter (prometheus-community) exposes NVMe and SATA SMART metrics on /metrics with a 60s default scrape and 10-min device rescan, Grafana dashboard 22604 ready-made, but ships no NVMe alerting rules (user-written PromQL) and needs privileged/root access to block devices.
stance_target: The Prometheus-exporter lane of the design space - what ha-linux-agent's MQTT approach avoids (external server, assembly, privilege model)
quoted_support: smartctl_exporter (prometheus-community) wraps smartctl JSON output and exposes NVMe and SATA SMART metrics on a /metrics endpoint. Default 60-second scrape interval with a 10-minute device rescan. ... No NVMe health alerting rules ship with the exporter; you write your own PromQL.

claim: Scrutiny (MIT, all-in-one Docker image) is a purpose-built SMART dashboard merging manufacturer metrics with Backblaze real-world failure rates for threshold grounding, but collects on a daily cron by default and requires the user to operate InfluxDB.
stance_target: Prior art for threshold-setting philosophy (observed failure rates vs arbitrary thresholds) applicable to the agent's alert tuning
scope_conditions: Scrutiny project, Docker deployments; vendor comparison page
quoted_support: Merges manufacturer SMART metrics with real-world failure rates from Backblaze, which grounds thresholds in observed data ... Collector runs on a daily cron schedule by default, so health data is not real-time. Requires InfluxDB for storage, adding operational overhead.

claim: Nagios check_smart (Napsty fork) uniquely supports drives behind hardware RAID controllers (MegaRAID, HP CCISS, Intel RAID) via smartctl, but Nagios provides no SMART trend data - it tells you a threshold was crossed, not that media errors doubled weekly.
stance_target: Trend data (history) as a differentiator an agent with local history or HA recorder integration provides
scope_conditions: Nagios/Icinga plugin ecosystem; vendor comparison page
quoted_support: The check_smart plugin (Napsty fork) monitors HDD, SSD, and NVMe drives via smartctl. Supports drives behind hardware RAID controllers (MegaRAID, HP CCISS, Intel RAID). ... Nagios tells you a drive crossed a threshold, not that its media error count has doubled every week for a month.
